params.question: What does suno.com offer, how is its product organised, and what does a private, original prompt-to-song app (MusicMake) need in order to cover the same kinds of jobs?

params.claim: Generating two takes per prompt lets people pick the better one, which hides the variance of generative models.
params.prediction: Each create action shows two results to choose from.

params.claim: A local open model (ACE-Step 1.5) plus Demucs covers the core jobs for a private app.
params.prediction: ACE-Step 1.5 offers text2music, cover (remix) and repaint (extend); Demucs gives 4 stems.

params.statement: The core job is one prompt in, a complete song with vocals, lyrics and production out; everything else (Studio, Voices, Remix, Stems, Custom Models) builds on a generated or uploaded track.
User controls named publicly are: style, things to leave out, vocal gender, an adventurousness-type slider and a style-influence slider, plus a simple prompt-only mode.
The Terms forbid reverse engineering, scraping, robots and building competing products, so only public, hand-read information is used and nothing is automated against suno.com.
ACE-Step 1.5 (MIT) covers text-to-song with vocals, remix (cover) and extend (repaint) through a local REST API on under 4 GB of VRAM; Demucs (MIT) covers stem splitting.
For a private app, the jobs worth covering first are: prompt to song, lyrics to song, two takes, extend, remix, stems, download, library with favourites, and a lyric helper.

params.text: Research and MVP are done.
